title: Multi-File AI Workflows
description: Learn to use AI for changes that span multiple files — migrations, refactors, and feature implementations across your codebase.

data.text: Single-file changes are easy — you see the impact immediately. Multi-file changes are harder because the impact is distributed across the codebase. Changing a data model might require updates in the API layer, the UI layer, the validation logic, and the tests. Missing any one of these leads to runtime errors. AI agents excel here because they can reason about the whole codebase at once.

The key to successful multi-file AI changes is to give the agent a complete picture of what needs to change and why. Instead of asking for changes file by file, describe the end state and let the agent figure out which files need updating. This produces more consistent results because the agent can maintain a global view of the changes.

data.title: Scenarios where multi-file AI workflows shine:
items: Migration: Changing from class components to functional components across a React app
Rename: Renaming a data model that appears in controllers, services, tests, and migrations
Refactor: Extracting a shared utility from duplicated logic across 10 files
Upgrade: Updating an API version across routes, clients, and documentation
Feature: Adding a new field to a model and propagating it through all layers

data.text: Using Cursor Composer for Multi-File Changes

Cursor Composer is the most capable tool for multi-file changes. Describe the end state you want, and Composer will propose changes across all relevant files. It shows a diff for each file and lets you accept or reject changes individually. Review each diff carefully — Composer may modify files you did not expect.

data.title: Review every diff
data.text: Multi-file changes can have cascading effects. A rename in one file might break an import in another. Always review the full diff, not just the files you expected to change. Look for unexpected modifications.

GitHub Copilot Workspace is a newer feature that lets you describe changes in plain language and see the proposed multi-file diff before applying. It is similar to Cursor Composer but integrated directly into the GitHub interface. Use it when you want to propose changes in a PR context without switching to your IDE.

data.title: A reliable workflow for complex multi-file changes:
items: Define the end state: 'I want the User model to use UUIDs instead of auto-increment integers'
Identify all affected files: models, migrations, controllers, tests, fixtures
Make the change incrementally: update the model, then the migration, then the code
Run tests after each step to catch issues early
If a step fails, paste the error back into the agent for a targeted fix
Do a final review of all changed files before committing

data.text: Multi-file AI changes can create merge conflicts if other developers are working on the same files. To minimize conflicts, keep AI-generated changes in a separate branch and rebase frequently. If conflicts occur, paste the conflict markers into the AI and ask for help resolving — the AI can often resolve straightforward conflicts automatically.

After a multi-file change, run the full test suite, not just the tests in the files you changed. Multi-file changes can break things in unexpected places — a rename in the model might break a test in the integration layer. Run all tests and verify the application still works end-to-end before opening a PR.

data.title: Multi-file migration prompt
data.content: "I want to migrate our User model from MongoDB to PostgreSQL. Here is the current User schema and all files that reference it: [paste schema + relevant files]. The new Prisma schema is: [paste schema]. Please update all files that reference the User model to use the new Prisma client. Preserve exact behavior including query patterns and error handling. Update all test files to use the new data access layer."

data.title: Commit incrementally
data.text: For complex multi-file changes, commit after each logical step (model change, migration, controller update, test updates). This makes it easier to revert if something goes wrong and gives you a clear history of what changed and why.

data.title: Multi-file AI workflows
points: Describe the end state, not individual file changes
Use Cursor Composer or Copilot Workspace for multi-file generation
Review every diff — multi-file changes have cascading effects
Run the full test suite after multi-file changes
